messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for hosted inference across shared-gpu pool 'shared-gpu-west-2' — p95 jumped from 220ms -> 1.1s; p99 from 420ms -> 3.8s. Streaming stalls increasing (connections with stalled chunks: 42). Auto-remediation not triggered (no quota exceed). Dashboard: https://console.redwood/infer/dashboards/latency#/shared-gpu-west-2
maya (oncall): Ack. paging @ashwin @jules. Can someone grab root cause?
ashwin (eng-sre): On it. collecting `svc=runtime` tail traces now. Starting `aggregate-latency-trace --since 10m --pool shared-gpu-west-2`
ashwin (eng-sre): early look: tail growth correlates with elevated NVMe read latencies on nodes gpunode-07..gpunode-09, IOPS spike ~4x. cgroup blkio rates for a few tenants are saturated.
jules (sre-lead): suspect noisy-tenant. Any heavy checkpoint/eviction/jobs around that time?
kevin (support): Customer-impact: two customers S-42 and S-77 reported streaming stalls (broken chunks, reconnects). S-42 has a high-traffic reranker workload right now. Logged on ticket #CS-4412.
ops (infra-bot): Node alerts: gpunode-07 nvme_latency_p99=176ms (baseline 12ms), cpu steal up, docker pids high. Top process on gpunode-07: container tenant:prod-s42 (cgroup id cg-0x3a).
maya (oncall): Quick mitigation options? Can we throttle the tenant, move to dedicated, or evict long-running jobs? Need mitigation with <5m blast radius.
ashwin (eng-sre): Running `cgset -r blkio.weight=100 /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/cg-0x3a` to deprioritize heavy IO tenant. Also preparing `runtime-ctl move-tenant --tenant prod-s42 --dest pool=dedicated-temp-1 --grace 30s` as a fallback if throttle doesn't help.
maya (oncall): Please run throttle first. Notify customers when we move.
ashwin (eng-sre): Throttle applied to prod-s42: `blkio.weight` lowered -> observed immediate drop in raw NVMe IOPS for that container. Monitoring..
ashwin (eng-sre): p95 improved 220ms -> 480ms within 60s. stalls reduced from 42 -> 18. But p99 still ~1.6s.
jules (sre-lead): Good. If p99 doesn't drop to <700ms in 3m, proceed with move to dedicated-temp-1. Make sure to set traffic drain to avoid state loss for streaming clients.
kevin (support): Notifying affected customers: "We're investigating streaming stalls; temporary throttling applied. We'll update if we migrate your workload. ETA 15-30m." Ticket updated for S-42/S-77.
ashwin (eng-sre): Second noisy tenant prod-batch-09 also showing high GPU mem copies -> kernel context switches jumped. Adding GPU SM cap for that container: `runtime-ctl set-gpu-share --container cg-0x4f --max-sm 0.25`
ops (infra-bot): Applied GPU SM cap for cg-0x4f. GPU utilization on gpunode-08 dropped 30%.
maya (oncall): Anyone seeing side effects? Watch for model OOMs or queueing.
ashwin (eng-sre): No OOMs so far. p99 trending down to 900ms. Streaming stall count 18 -> 6 over last 4m.
jules (sre-lead): Remediation looks effective. Root cause summary so far: multi-tenant NVMe IO contention from batch/eviction jobs + unthrottled GPU memory copy spikes causing tail stalls. cgroup blkio weighting and GPU-share caps helped. Need postmortem confirmation (logs + fio tests).
ashwin (eng-sre): Collecting `iostat -x 1 60` and kernel block traces from gpunode-07..09, saving to /mnt/incident/1819001234/. Also capturing docker stats and nvprof traces for the heavy containers.
kevin (support): Customer note: S-42 says they saw 10% error rate for streaming chunk failures during the window. Will offer a credit after incident wrap per policy.
maya (oncall): Who's owning follow-up: long term fixes? Ideas: enforce default blkio caps on shared pool tenants, detect NVMe pressure and auto-evict noisy tenants, better API-level tenant QoS.
jules (sre-lead): I'll own the postmortem and action items. @ashwin can you run a repro on a staging node with a simulated batch IO workload + streaming clients? We need thresholds and an automatic mitigation (auto-throttle or transparent move).
ashwin (eng-sre): Yep, will reproduce in staging. Planning a stress job: fio random-read with parallel jobs + synthetic streaming workload for 20m. Will repo commands to run.
ashwin (eng-sre): repro plan (snippet):
```
# on staging node
fio --name=burst --ioengine=libaio --rw=randread --bs=128k --numjobs=8 --size=20G --iodepth=32 --direct=1 &
python3 tools/sim_streamers.py --clients 200 --payload 4k --rate 80
```
Run with/without `blkio.weight=100` to measure tail.
maya (oncall): Good. For now, we remain in incident mitigation state. Handoff scheduled in 40m to next oncall. Who's taking the handoff?
jules (sre-lead): @maya please handoff to @ashwin for the next shift; I will coordinate postmortem and customers.
maya (oncall): Handoff to ashwin accepted. Action items for next oncall: keep throttles in place, watch p99 < 700ms, finalize move for any remaining noisy tenant, collect perf traces, update CS tickets.
ashwin (eng-sre): Acknowledged. I'll also enable an alert rule for NVMe p99 > 100ms per node and `blkio.weight` anomalous drops.
kevin (support): I'll queue outgoing comms: updated customer note and set a follow-up reminder in 24h.
ops (infra-bot): Autoscaler suggestion: spare capacity in dedicated-temp-1 is 2 GPUs. If we need to move more tenants, recommend increasing pool to 6 GPUs.
maya (oncall): OK. Closing mitigation loop: throttles + gpu-share caps applied; partial tenant migration ready if needed; customer comms sent. Moving to monitoring state; escalate if p99 rises.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated -> monitoring. severity=sev2. impacted_customers=[S-42, S-77]. start_ts=1819001234. current_p99=640ms. next_update=1819003500.
maya (oncall): Logging this thread into incident tracker and will attach traces. Thanks everyone.
ashwin (eng-sre): Uploading traces/logs to /mnt/incident/1819001234/trace.tar.gz now. Will post repro results in #eng-sre-stress once complete.
jules (sre-lead): Postmortem assigned. Initial RCA: noisy tenant I/O + GPU memory copy storms leading to IO queueing and streaming tail latencies. Remediation proposals: default blkio caps, tenant telemetry to detect heavy IO patterns, auto-evict policy, and increase dedicated pool min capacity.
maya (oncall): Handoff complete. Leaving thread open for traces and PM notes.
customer-success: Noted. We'll coordinate comms for credits if CS requests.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: closed_by=jules, closed_ts=1819003500, duration=2266s, severity=sev2, summary="Noisy neighbor NVMe/GPU contention caused p99 tail latency spikes; mitigated with cgroup throttles and GPU-share caps."
